title: Russell US Style indexes — conditional capping check effective at the open of 2027-06-30 (24% / 4.8%-above-48% test struck on the 2027-06-25 close), the one quarter whose own capping review does not take effect until AFTER the test is struck
source: EST: owner-published, re-fetched and re-extracted independently this session from THREE documents, two of them primaries neither sibling in this family read for this purpose. (1) FTSE Russell, "Frequently Asked Questions -- Russell US Equity Indexes", July 2026 (lseg.com dam policy-documents, ftse-faq-document-russell-us-equity-2026.pdf, HTTP 200, 198,134 bytes, 19 content streams inflated in-session 2026-09-08 -- byte count and stream count reproduce both siblings). ITS JUNE 2026 COLUMN IS THE FINDING, AND NEITHER SIBLING QUOTED IT: verbatim, "Russell US Style Capping Cut-Off Date | 17 June 2026", "Review Effective Date (open of) | 29 June 2026", "Russell US Style Quarter-end Capping Cut-Off Date | 25 June 2026", "Russell US Style Quarter-end Capping Effective Date (open of, if applicable) | 30 June 2026". In March, September and December the review's effective date PRECEDES the quarter-end cut-off (23 Mar < 26 Mar; 21 Sep < 25 Sep; 14 Dec < 28 Dec). In JUNE ALONE it follows it -- 29 June against a test struck on the 25 June close. (2) FTSE Russell, "Capping Methodology Guide", v5.4, September 2026 (capping-methodology-guide.pdf, HTTP 200, 652,008 bytes, 62 streams inflated), section 4.8.6: every Russell US Style row reads frequency "Monthly", price date "T-3", effective date "Last business day of each month" carrying footnote 3, trigger "No company is greater than 24%, and all companies that have a weight greater than 4.8% in aggregate are no more than 48% of the index", scheme "Rule 4.2/RIC 22.5/45" -- the December sibling's row-level correction, reproduced here from an independent extraction. FOOTNOTE 3 WAS READ VERBATIM AND DOES NOT FIRE IN 2027: "If Russell Reconstitution is scheduled to take effect after the close of the last business day in June, meaning it is effective for the open of the first business day in July, then the quarter-end capping check will not be performed. In such cases, the standard application of capping at the quarterly reviews will be applied, and the capping adjustments already announced will be made effective concurrently with the Russell Reconstitution." Russell reconstitution 2027 implements after the close of Friday 2027-06-25 and is effective at the open of Monday 2027-06-28 (russell-reconstitution-2027-06-25 in this calendar, itself derived from ground rules v7.2 by a different lane), and the last business day of June 2027 is Wednesday 2027-06-30, so the exemption is inapplicable. Enumerated mechanically this session for every June 2005-2040, the exemption fires in exactly 4 of 36 years -- 2013, 2019, 2024 and 2030 -- which are precisely the Junes beginning on a Saturday; the next one is 2030, not 2027. (3) NYSE, "Holidays and Trading Hours" (nyse.com/markets/hours-calendars), fetched direct 2026-09-08 (HTTP 200, 109,180 bytes), whose 2027 column reads "Friday, June 18 (Juneteenth National Independence Day observed)" -- a full closure that removes one session from every June 2027 count below and is corroborated by this repo's own src/domain/market-calendar.ts. THE 2027 DATES ARE RULE-DERIVED, NOT PUBLISHED, and the derivation was tested rather than asserted: review effective open = the Monday after the quarter's implementation Friday, and the style capping cut-off = that Monday minus 12 calendar days. That pair reproduces ALL FOUR published 2026 columns to the day (11 Mar/23 Mar, 17 Jun/29 Jun, 9 Sep/21 Sep, 2 Dec/14 Dec), so June 2027 reads cut-off Wednesday 2027-06-16, review effective open Monday 2027-06-28, quarter-end cut-off Friday 2027-06-25 (T-3 from Wednesday 2027-06-30), effective open Wednesday 2027-06-30. Filed estimate on the four counts this family always records: a proposal is estimate by contract and this canonical file inherits that posture, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, the confirmed-tier prefixes in market-events-data.ts have no member for an index owner's own published methodology, and the FAQ's own schedule table carries "NOTE: Dates may be subject to change. Clients will be notified of any changes." Conditional by construction -- the FAQ says "If no breach is identified, no changes are made." Canonical file written by this event's own initial research after reading in full the single proposal carrying this id, checked 2026-09-08
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THIS EVENT'S OWN INITIAL RESEARCH (2026-09-08), which read proposals/russell-style-quarter-end-capping-effective-2027-06-30.from-fhfa-hpi-2027-06-29.json in full first, then re-fetched every owner document rather than inheriting its readings. Ledger: docs/research/events/russell-style-quarter-end-capping-effective-2027-06-30.md. THE PROPOSAL ASKED THIS LANE TO SETTLE THE MONTHLY-VERSUS-QUARTERLY FREQUENCY CONFLICT. It is already settled -- the 2026-12-31 sibling settled it a session earlier and this session reproduced its row-level reading independently (guide v5.4 says Monthly for every Russell US Style row; the quarterly wording belongs to the FTSE Emerging ex China rows). What this session found instead is that the conflict MATTERS HERE IN A WAY IT DID NOT MATTER THERE, and that is this entry's reason to exist. THE JUNE INVERSION: in March, September and December the quarterly style capping review takes effect BEFORE the quarter-end test's price date, so the test reads a freshly recapped index and the drift window is 11, 12 and 17 sessions respectively. In June it does not. The review is effective at the open of 2027-06-28 -- concurrently with reconstitution, exactly as footnote 3 describes -- three sessions AFTER the test is struck on the 2027-06-25 close. So the June test reads an index its own quarter's review has not yet recapped, and the cohort's drift is measured from whatever reset was last actually IN FORCE. THAT FORK IS WORTH 20x, MEASURED THIS SESSION on five years of daily bars (1,253 usable sessions, 2021-09-09 to 2026-09-04, Yahoo, fetched this session): inheriting the siblings' cut-off anchor mechanically gives a 6-session window and 27/1,247 = 2.17%; the in-force reading under the guide's MONTHLY cadence (March quarter-end, April and May month-end checks modelled as conditional resets) gives 223/1,179 = 18.91%; the in-force reading under the FAQ's QUARTERLY cadence, where only the March quarter-end check can reset, gives 512/1,179 = 43.43%. No owner document read this session says which index the T-3 check reads, so the honest output is a band, not a number -- and footnote 3's own words ("the capping adjustments already announced will be made effective concurrently with the Russell Reconstitution") are the strongest evidence for the in-force end of it. Under every reading the call is the same refusal, which is why impact stays low. A SECOND FINDING, AND IT IS A NEGATIVE ONE ABOUT THIS FAMILY'S OWN ARITHMETIC: this session re-implemented the siblings' base-rate method from scratch and DOES NOT REPRODUCE their absolute levels. Same rule, same 48%/45% thresholds, same cohort, same five-year bar set: the September sibling's 12-session post-reset case reads 98/1,241 = 7.90% here against its recorded 50/1,243 = 4.02%, and the December sibling's 17-session case reads 176/1,236 = 14.24% against its recorded 96/1,237 = 7.76%. The no-reset cases diverge too (12-session 35.05% vs 29.07%; 17-session 39.00% vs 35.65%). Five implementation variants were tried (adjusted versus raw closes, Alphabet as one line versus two, IWY versus IWF versus SPY as the benchmark) and none closes the gap. The December ledger reads its agreement with the September one as "the cross-check that the method was rebuilt rather than copied"; a genuinely independent third rebuild disagrees with both, so that cross-check does not carry the weight it was given. The ORDERING is robust in every variant -- June's window is the shortest and December's the longest -- and the call rests on the ordering, not on the level. THIRD, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED: drifting IWY's cohort backwards from 46.81% (holdings 2026-08-27) on this session's own bars implies 44.62% at the 2026-06-17 review cut-off and 43.97% at the 2026-06-25 quarter-end test -- BELOW the 45% cap. The June 2026 review had nothing to recap and the June 2026 test was nowhere near 48%, so the most recent June instance is a null that discriminates nothing between the anchors. It also means the cohort spent mid-2026 under the cap and has only recently crossed it, which is a caveat on every "reset to 45%" starting assumption in this family, including this one. SCOPE AND SIZE, RE-VERIFIED FROM THE VENDOR THIS SESSION: the iShares product screener returns IWF $126.03B, IWD $84.06B, IWP $19.63B, IWY $15.94B, IWS $15.67B, IWO $14.70B, IWN $14.61B, IWX $3.98B = $294.61B, reproducing both siblings. IWY's over-4.8% company cohort (Alphabet's two lines combined per the guide's own rule) reads 46.81% and IWF's 44.47% on holdings dated 2026-08-27, identical to the December sibling's readings. The single-name leg is dead by a wide margin (NVDA 16.21% in IWY against a 22.5% cap and a 24% trigger). A fired recap moves about 3pp of IWY's $15.94B, roughly $478M, across five mega caps. Impact low and symbols deliberately EMPTY on the family's measured grounds: no house playbook is index-flow-keyed (trade-playbooks.md and multi-symbol-sweep.md re-grepped this session for rebalanc|reconstitution|russell|capping|index.flow|IWF|IWY -> zero hits in both), and an ETF proxy in symbols would make the deterministic screen trip on mega-cap beta. THE CORRIDOR IS THE THINNEST THIS FAMILY HAS SEEN: 5 tracked events within five days (29 around the September instance, 14 around the December one) -- russell-reconstitution-2027-06-25 on the test's own price date, consumer-confidence-2027-06-29 and fhfa-hpi-2027-06-29 the session a recap would trade, and fomc-minutes-2027-06-30 plus sp-select-sector-secondary-reweight-2027-06-30 on the effective date itself. Nothing here licenses an entry.
